questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Roshni always want (1)/ to get the best of facilities (2)/ whether she deserves it or not. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Here, concept of subject-verb agreement is brought under consideration. Since, **Roshni **is a third person singular noun. Hence, according to sub-verb agreement, singular verb should be used. Thus, replace **want **with **wants. **Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

Note :- Number of verb is not affected from adverb.

**Correct sentence - **Roshni always wants to get the best of facilities whether she deserves it or not.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

I insisted but neither Praveen or his (1)/ friend Bharat is ready (2)/ to work on holiday. (3)/ No Error(4)
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Here, concept of coordinating conjunction is brought under consideration. There are some conjunctions that are always used in pairs like either....or, neither......nor, so....and, as...as, etc. Clearly, replace **or **with **nor. **Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **I insisted but neither Praveen nor his friend Bharat is ready to work on holiday.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

My house is adjacent _____ Central park.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Here, concept of preposition is brought under consideration. There are certain words which take fixed preposition after them.

For example :- fond of; agreeable to; along with; in addition to; in case of; adjacent to; etc. 

Clearly, option 1 i.e. **to **is the correct answer. 

**Correct sentence - **My house is adjacent *to* Central park.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

I prefer walking _____ jogging because I enjoy the gentle exercise of walking much more than jogging.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

Here, concept of preposition is brought under consideration. Verb **prefer **takes a fixed preposition **to **after it. Hence, option 3 i.e. **to **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **I prefer walking to jogging because I enjoy the gentle exercise of walking much more than jogging.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Rohan _____ for this company since 2007.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Here, concept of present perfect continuous tense is being focused. Words since and for are used in a sentence to show an action which has already started and still going on. They are used in case of perfect continuous tense. Following is the pattern for present continuous tense:- Sub + has/have + been + V4 + Object.

Hence, option 1 i.e. **has been working **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **Rohan has been working for this company since 2007.

questions.question:

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Piquant
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (3) i.e. "Appealing".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Piquant (मसालेदार) - Having a pleasantly sharp taste or appetizing flavor; interestingly provocative or stimulating.
 
 
• Example: The salsa had a piquant flavor that made the dish stand out.
 
 
 
• Appealing (आकर्षक) - Attractive or interesting.
 
 
• Example: The idea of working from home is very appealing to many people.
 
 
 
• The word "Appealing" is similar in meaning to "Piquant" because both describe something that is interestingly provocative, stimulating, or attractive in a way that draws attention or interest.

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Appealing".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Distressing (परेशान करने वाला) - Causing anxiety, sorrow, or pain; upsetting.
 
 
• Example: The news of the accident was quite distressing to everyone involved.
 
 
 
• Gabble (बड़बड़ाना) - Talk rapidly and unintelligibly; utter meaningless sounds.
 
 
• Example: Nervous and excited, she began to gabble her words almost incomprehensibly.
 
 
 
• Pliable (लचीला) - Easily bent; flexible or easily influenced.
 
 
• Example: The soft clay was pliable in the artist's hands.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

No sooner **(he had returned home then)** his grandparents felt happy.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Did he return home than.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• 'No sooner' and 'than' are **correlative conjunctions** i.e., they are always used in **pairs**.

 
 
• For example: **No sooner** did I reach the station** than **the train left. (Hence, options 3) and 4) are incorrect as 'than' is not used.)
 
 
 
• When we use an **adverb** with negative meaning (e.g. never, scarcely, hardly, **no sooner)** in front position for emphasis, we **interchange** the **subject** and the **verb**. The verb is used before the subject, in this case. This is the **rule of inversion**.
 
• The format of '**No sooner…than'** is: **No sooner + did + Subject + V1 + than + rest of the sentence**.
 
 
• For example: No sooner did the bell ring than I opened it.
 
 
 
• Only option 1) follows the above mentioned structure of the sentence, which is grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is:** ***No sooner **did he return home than**__ his grandparents felt happy.*
